description: Mendelevium is a synthetic chemical element with symbol Md and atomic number 101. It is a metallic radioactive transuranium element in the actinide series and the first element by atomic number that currently cannot be produced in macroscopic quantities by neutron bombardment of lighter elements. It is the thirteenth actinide, the ninth transuranic element, and the first transfermium, named after Dmitri Mendeleev, the father of the periodic table.
uses: There are currently no uses for mendelevium outside basic scientific research, as only small amounts are produced.
characteristics: Mendelevium has a dominant +3 oxidation state but also a +2 oxidation state accessible in solution, with a +1 state also reported but not yet confirmed. All known isotopes have short half-lives. Mendelevium metal has not been prepared in bulk and is predicted to be divalent with a metallic radius around 194±10 pm, a melting point estimated at 800°C, and density around 10.3±0.7 g/cm³.
